title: 全波整流电压的平均值、有效值和谐波
statement: 220 V、50 Hz 的市电经理想全波整流后，加在 R = 100 Ω 的负载上：u = 220√2 |cos(100πt)| V。
整流后的电压周期是 T = 10 ms，基波频率 f_1 = 100 Hz，它的傅里叶级数为
u = \frac{2U_m}{π} + \frac{4U_m}{π}(\frac{1}{3}cos ω_{1}t − \frac{1}{15}cos 2ω_{1}t + \frac{1}{35}cos 3ω_{1}t − …)，U_m = 220√2 V，ω_1 = 2π × 100 rad/s（计算取到 49 次谐波）。
求 u 的平均值、有效值、基波（100 Hz）振幅，以及负载吸收的平均功率。

questions.explain: |cos| 的平方和 cos² 相同，所以整流不改变有效值：U = U_m/√2 = 220 V。

questions.ask: 100 Hz 分量（基波）的振幅 U_1m = ?
questions.explain: U_1m = 4U_m/(3π) ≈ 132.0 V。整流后的电压里没有 50 Hz 分量，最低的交流分量是 100 Hz。

questions.ask: 负载吸收的平均功率 P = ?
questions.explain: P = U²/R = 220²/100 = 484 W，和不整流时一样（电阻不在乎电流方向）。

questions.ask: 波形因数 K_f = U/U_0 约为多少？
choiceExplain: 只有直流（或方波）的有效值才等于平均值。
1.41 是正弦波的峰值因数 U_m/U。
questions.explain: K_f = 220/198.1 ≈ 1.11 = π/(2√2)。用“全波整流式”仪表测正弦量时，表内就是用平均值乘 1.11 来显示有效值的。

hints: 平均值就是级数的常数项；有效值可以不用级数，直接从 u² 的平均值求。
u² = U_m² cos²(100πt)，它和整流之前完全一样。
基波振幅直接从级数读出：\frac{4U_m}{π}·\frac{1}{3}；平均功率 P = U²/R。
solution: **2. 有效值。** u² = U_m² cos²(100πt) 与整流前相同，所以 U = U_m/√2 = **220 V**。
**检查：** 用谐波求有效值：U² = U_0² + Σ U_km²/2 ≈ 198.1² + 132.0²/2 + 26.41²/2 + … ≈ 220²，与第 2 步一致（直流分量贡献了 81%）。

en.title: Full-wave rectified voltage: average, rms value and harmonics
statement: 220 V, 50 Hz mains is full-wave rectified by ideal diodes and applied to a load R = 100 Ω: u = 220√2 |cos(100πt)| V.
The rectified voltage has period T = 10 ms and fundamental frequency f_1 = 100 Hz; its Fourier series is
u = \frac{2U_m}{π} + \frac{4U_m}{π}(\frac{1}{3}cos ω_{1}t − \frac{1}{15}cos 2ω_{1}t + \frac{1}{35}cos 3ω_{1}t − …), U_m = 220√2 V, ω_1 = 2π × 100 rad/s (harmonics up to the 49th are kept).
Find the average value and rms value of u, the amplitude of the fundamental (100 Hz) and the average power absorbed by the load.
hints: The average value is the constant term of the series; the rms value can be found without the series, from the average of u².
u² = U_m² cos²(100πt), exactly as before rectification.
Read the fundamental's amplitude from the series: \frac{4U_m}{π}·\frac{1}{3}; the average power is P = U²/R.
solution: **1. Average value.** The constant term U_0 = 2U_m/π = 2 × 220√2/π = **198.1 V**. Or integrate directly: \frac{1}{T}∫_{0}^{T} U_m|cos(100πt)| dt = 2U_m/π.
**2. rms value.** u² = U_m² cos²(100πt) is the same as before rectification, so U = U_m/√2 = **220 V**.
**3. Fundamental.** The f_1 = 100 Hz component has U_1m = 4U_m/(3π) = **132.0 V**; the 2nd harmonic (200 Hz) has 4U_m/(15π) = 26.41 V — the harmonics fall off quickly.
**Check:** rms value from the harmonics: U² = U_0² + Σ U_km²/2 ≈ 198.1² + 132.0²/2 + 26.41²/2 + … ≈ 220², as in step 2 (the DC component contributes 81 %).

questions.explain: |cos| squared is the same as cos², so rectification does not change the rms value: U = U_m/√2 = 220 V.

questions.ask: Amplitude of the 100 Hz component (the fundamental), U_1m = ?
questions.explain: U_1m = 4U_m/(3π) ≈ 132.0 V. The rectified voltage has no 50 Hz component; its lowest AC component is at 100 Hz.

questions.ask: Average power absorbed by the load, P = ?
questions.explain: P = U²/R = 220²/100 = 484 W, the same as without the rectifier (a resistor does not care about the direction of the current).

questions.ask: The form factor K_f = U/U_0 is about
choiceExplain: Only DC (or a square wave) has its rms value equal to its average.
1.41 is the crest factor U_m/U of a sine wave.
0.90 is U_0/U, the other way round.
questions.explain: K_f = 220/198.1 ≈ 1.11 = π/(2√2). A rectifier-type meter measuring a sine wave shows the average times 1.11 as its rms reading.
